newsitem.title: USA: MGI files with FDA for new Salagen use.
newsitem.headline: MGI files with FDA for new Salagen use.

text.p: MGI Pharma Inc said it submitted a supplemental new drug application for Salagen tablets to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

The submission requests permission to market Salagen as a treatment for the symptoms of keratoconjunctivitis sicca (dry eyes) and xerostomia (dry mouth) associated with Sjogren's Syndrome, the pharmaceuticals company said.

Chief executive Charles Blitzer said, "Based on the significant improvements in patients' symptoms found in our Phase III clinical studies, we are eager to expand Salagen's label to include the Sjogren's indication."

Sjogren's Syndrome is a chronic disease in which the body's own immune system attacks moisture producing glands, particularly the salivary and tear glands, causing them to lose their ability to produce saliva and tears.
The resulting dryness can cause severe discomfort in the mouth and eyes. Sjogren's affects about 200,000 Americans, most of whom are women over the age of 50, MGI said.
Salagen has been marketed in the United Stats since 1994 as a treatment for dry mouth caused by radiation when used to treat head and neck cancer.
The drug works by stimulating moisture producing glands throughout the body, including the salivary and tear glands.
